bib.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models", Dhuliawala, Komeili, Xu, Raileanu, Li, Celikyilmaz, Weston (Meta AI; ETH Zurich). Preprint: the only venue mark on the PDF is "arXiv:2309.11495v2 [cs.CL] 25 Sep 2023". 2023.
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/08-eval/sources/dhuliawala-2023-chain-verification-reduces-hallucination-large.pdf

COVERAGE: 19 of 19 pages, 51,241 of 51,241 chars. Body pp1-9, references pp10-12 (skimmed for origins), appendices pp13-19 (Fig 3, prompt templates Tables 5-9, ChatGPT screenshots). The screenshots in Figs 4-8 are images, so only their captions were read.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: A model answers short, isolated verification questions far more accurately than it states the same facts inside a long answer.
  number: ~17% vs ~70%
  setup: Wikidata list task, Llama 65B few-shot, 56 questions
  quote: "only ∼17% of the Llama few-shot baseline answer entities are correct in list-based questions. However, when querying each individual entity via a verification question, we find ∼70% are correctly answered."
  where: p9

- claim: Explicit per-fact cross-checking (factor+revise) gives the best longform factuality.
  number: FActScore 55.9 (few-shot) → 60.8 (joint) → 63.7 (factored) → 71.4 (factor+revise); average facts 16.6 → 12.3
  setup: biography generation (Min et al. 2023 benchmark), Llama 65B, greedy decoding, FActScore computed automatically by "Instruct-Llama" with retrieval; n not stated
  quote: "FACTSCORE increases 28% (55.9 → 71.4) from the few-shot baseline, with again only a relatively small reduction in average number of facts provided (16.6 → 12.3)."
  where: p8, Table 3 p7

- claim: Answering verification questions without the draft in context beats answering them jointly.
  number: Wikidata precision 0.17 baseline, 0.29 joint, 0.36 two-step, 0.32 factored; Wiki-Category 0.12 / 0.15 / 0.21 / 0.22
  setup: Llama 65B; 56 Wikidata questions (~600 gold entities each) and 55 QUEST questions (~8 answers each); micro-averaged precision
  quote: "more than doubles the precision from the Llama 65B few-shot baseline for the Wikidata task (from 0.17 to 0.36) ... (negatives: 2.95 → 0.68) ... (positives: 0.59 → 0.38)."
  where: p7, Table 1 p6

- claim: Open questions beat yes/no questions, and model-written questions beat templated ones.
  number: factored precision 0.16 rule-based, 0.19 yes/no, 0.22 general; joint 0.13 / 0.15 / 0.15
  setup: Wiki-Category task only, Llama 65B
  quote: "Rule-based questions 0.13 0.16 ... yes/no questions 0.15 0.19 general questions 0.15 0.22"
  where: Table 4, p8

- claim: Yes/no verification invites agreement (acquiescence), though the evidence for this is anecdotal.
  number: none
  setup: ChatGPT screenshots only
  quote: "the model tends to agree with facts in a yes/no question format whether they are right or wrong."
  where: p9; Fig 8 p19

- claim: Closed-book QA improves modestly.
  number: F1 0.39 → 0.46 (joint) → 0.48 (factored); precision 0.40 → 0.50, recall 0.38 → 0.46
  setup: MultiSpanQA, 418 factoid questions, answers up to 3 tokens per item, Llama 65B
  quote: "We observe a 23% improvement in F1 over the few-shot baseline (0.39 → 0.48)"
  where: p7, Table 2

- claim: Chain-of-thought and instruction tuning did not help on these tasks.
  number: Llama 2 70B Chat FActScore 41.3 zero-shot, 41.1 CoT; Wikidata precision 0.12 vs 0.08
  setup: zero-shot, with NER post-processing on list tasks
  quote: "Standard chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting also fails to improve the results for these tasks."
  where: p8

- claim: CoVe on Llama 65B outscores the retrieval-based PerplexityAI overall, but not on very rare facts.
  number: 71.4 vs 61.6 (ChatGPT 58.7, InstructGPT 41.1; these three are taken from prior work)
  quote: "PerplexityAI still outperforms CoVe for very rare facts where retrieval is essential"
  where: p8, Fig 2 p7

LIMITS
- Conceded by the authors: hallucinations are reduced, not removed; only "directly stated factual inaccuracies" are addressed, not reasoning errors or opinions; extra token cost; the gain is capped by what the model knows; no retrieval or tools tested.
- Not shown:
  - CoVe is a generation-time correction method, not a judge or evaluator. It never measures verification accuracy against human labels, so using it to support judge design is an inference.
  - Precision gains cost recall of correct items: Wikidata positives fall 0.59 → 0.38 (about a third) and biography facts 16.6 → 12.3. The paper calls this "relatively small".
  - No confidence intervals, significance tests or seeds, on small test sets (56, 55, 418; biography n unstated).
  - One base model (Llama 65B). The baseline and CoVe use different few-shot prompts.
  - Two-step is reported only for the list tasks, and factor+revise only for biographies.
  - The yes/no ablation is on one task, where the joint variant shows no difference (0.15 vs 0.15).
  - The "~70%" figure has no table behind it.
  - FActScore is itself an automated LLM-plus-retrieval metric.
  - Cost and latency are not measured.
- Dated: Llama 65B, Llama 2 and 2023 ChatGPT. No evidence for current models.

BUILDS ON
- Radhakrishnan et al. (2023), factored decomposition; the "factored" name is adopted from it.
- Min et al. (2023), FActScore and the biography benchmark.
- Cohen et al. (2023), LM vs LM cross-examination.
- Manakul et al. (2023), SelfCheckGPT.
- Wei et al. (2022), chain-of-thought.
- Madaan et al. (2023), Self-Refine; Press et al. (2022).
- Zhang et al. (2023), hallucination snowballing.
- Holtzman et al. (2019), repetition.
- Li et al. (2022), MultiSpanQA; Malaviya et al. (2023), QUEST.

CODE (prompt template, Table 9, p16, verbatim)
```
Context: <Original Fact>.
From another source,
<output of execute verification step: Q + A>
Response: CONSISTENT. <Consistent fact>
...
Response: INCONSISTENT.
...
Response: PARTIALLY CONSISTENT. <Consistent part>
```
Table 8 (p15) notes the model "is told that this information comes from 'another source'".

FIGURES
- Figure 1, p2: "Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) method..." It shows the four steps on one query (politicians born in New York), where the draft lists Hillary Clinton and the isolated question "Where was Hillary Clinton born?" returns Chicago. It conveys both decomposition and the reason for hiding the draft faster than prose does. Figure 3 (p13) is the alternative if the per-claim tick/cross check is wanted for the grounding note.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is clean, with no embedded instructions.
- Minor artefacts: small-caps render as "C OVE" / "F ACTSCORE", and Figure 2's axis labels are interleaved into the p7 text.
- Figure 2's per-rarity values are plot-only and not extractable, so none are reported.
- "28%" and "23%" are relative improvements as printed, not percentage points.
